subject: ela
intro: Clear and coherent writing matches its audience, develops its ideas, stays on topic, and uses precise wording. For each item, read the short sentence or sentence pair and answer the question.

items.prompt:
A student is writing a note to ask the school principal for permission to start a chess club. Which opening best fits this formal request to a school authority?
A) Hey, can we make a chess club? It would be so cool.
B) Dear Principal Adams, I am writing to request permission to start a chess club.
items.answer: B) Dear Principal Adams, I am writing to request permission to start a chess club.

steps: The audience is the principal, a school authority, and the purpose is a serious request, so the tone should be formal and respectful.
Option A uses casual, slangy language ('Hey', 'so cool') that does not fit a formal request to a principal.
Option B greets the principal by name and states the request respectfully, matching the task, purpose, and audience.

items.prompt:
Read the wordy sentence: 'Our bus came late on account of the fact that there was a lot of traffic.' Which revision states the same idea most clearly?
A) Our bus came late because of traffic.
B) The thing about the bus was that it came late, and that was because of all the traffic that there was.
items.answer: A) Our bus came late because of traffic.

steps: Clear writing states the idea precisely without padding or extra words.
Option B is even wordier and repeats the idea, which does not make the writing clearer.
Option A keeps the full meaning but cuts the padding, so it is the clearest revision.

items.prompt:
Read this short paragraph about planting a garden: 'First, dig a small hole. Next, place the seed inside. My favorite color is green. Then cover the seed with soil.' Which sentence should be removed to keep the writing on topic?
A) Next, place the seed inside.
B) My favorite color is green.
items.answer: B) My favorite color is green.

steps: The paragraph explains the steps of planting a garden, so every sentence should connect to that topic.
Option A is a real step in planting and belongs in the paragraph.
Option B is off topic because a favorite color has nothing to do with how to plant a garden, so it should be removed.

items.prompt:
A student is texting a close friend to invite them over after school. Which message best matches this casual purpose and audience?
A) I hereby formally request your presence at my residence following the conclusion of the school day.
B) Want to come over after school today?
items.answer: B) Want to come over after school today?

steps: The audience is a close friend and the purpose is a casual invitation, so a relaxed, friendly tone fits best.
Option A is overly formal and stiff, which does not match a text to a friend.
Option B is friendly and simple, matching the casual task and audience.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence: 'Our town should build a new library.' Which sentence best develops this idea with a clear, relevant detail?
A) A new library would give students a quiet place to study and free access to books.
B) Libraries are buildings.
items.answer: A) A new library would give students a quiet place to study and free access to books.

steps: Developing an idea means adding a specific, relevant detail or reason that supports it.
Option B just restates that libraries exist and gives no reason to build one, so it does not develop the idea.
Option A adds a clear reason (a quiet study place and free books), which supports the claim and develops the idea.

items.prompt:
Read this mostly formal sentence pair from a science report: 'The plants in the sunlight grew taller than the plants in the dark. This result was super legit, no cap.' Which revision of the second sentence keeps the tone consistent?
A) This result was reliable and clearly supported by the data.
B) Honestly, this result was totally awesome and amazing.
items.answer: A) This result was reliable and clearly supported by the data.

steps: The report uses a formal tone, so the second sentence should also be formal to keep the style consistent.
Option B uses casual, excited language ('totally awesome and amazing') that still clashes with the formal report.
Option A uses formal wording that matches the rest of the report, so the tone stays consistent.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence: 'The new park has a lot of nice stuff in it.' Which revision is clearer and more precise?
A) The new park has things in it that are nice.
B) The new park has a playground, a walking trail, and a picnic area.
items.answer: B) The new park has a playground, a walking trail, and a picnic area.

steps: Precise writing names specific details instead of using vague words like 'stuff' or 'things'.
Option A still uses the vague word 'things', so it is not more precise.
Option B replaces 'nice stuff' with specific features, making the sentence clear and precise.

items.prompt:
A student is writing a thank-you letter to a guest speaker who visited the class. Which sentence best fits this polite, formal purpose?
A) Thank you for taking the time to speak with our class about your work.
B) Thanks for showing up, that was kinda cool I guess.
items.answer: A) Thank you for taking the time to speak with our class about your work.

steps: A thank-you letter to a guest has a polite, formal purpose, so the tone should be respectful.
Option B is casual and lukewarm ('kinda cool I guess'), which does not fit a sincere thank-you letter.
Option A is polite and appreciative, matching the purpose and audience.

items.prompt:
Read this short paragraph about a soccer game: 'Our team scored in the first minute. We kept the lead the whole game. I really like pizza. We won by two goals.' Which sentence should be removed to keep the writing on topic?
A) We kept the lead the whole game.
B) I really like pizza.

steps: The paragraph is about a soccer game, so each sentence should connect to that game.
Option A is about the game and belongs in the paragraph.
Option B is about liking pizza, which has nothing to do with the soccer game, so it breaks the topic and should be removed.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence pair: 'I went to the store. I bought milk, bread, and eggs.' Is the tone of this writing formal or casual?
A) Formal
B) Casual

steps: Tone is the level of formality in the writing.
These sentences use simple, everyday wording with no formal or technical language.
That plain, conversational style is casual, so the answer is casual rather than formal.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence: 'Recycling is good.' Which sentence best develops this idea with a clear, relevant reason?
A) Recycling reduces waste by turning used materials into new products.
B) Recycling is a good thing to do.
items.answer: A) Recycling reduces waste by turning used materials into new products.

steps: Developing an idea means adding a specific reason that supports it.
Option B just repeats that recycling is good and gives no reason, so it does not develop the idea.
Option A explains how recycling helps (it reduces waste), which supports and develops the claim.

items.prompt:
A student is writing a formal email to a teacher to ask about a missed assignment. Which greeting best fits this formal purpose and audience?
A) Yo Mr. Lee, what did I miss lol?
B) Dear Mr. Lee, I would like to ask about the assignment I missed.
items.answer: B) Dear Mr. Lee, I would like to ask about the assignment I missed.

steps: The audience is a teacher and the email is a formal request, so the greeting should be respectful.
Option A is slangy ('Yo', 'lol'), which does not fit a formal email to a teacher.
Option B greets the teacher respectfully and states the request clearly, matching the formal purpose and audience.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence: 'The dog did a thing in the yard.' Which revision is clearer and more precise?
A) The dog dug a hole in the yard.
B) The dog did something out in the yard area.
items.answer: A) The dog dug a hole in the yard.

steps: Precise writing names exactly what happened instead of using vague words like 'a thing'.
Option B still uses vague wording ('did something'), so it is not clearer.
Option A states exactly what the dog did (dug a hole), making the sentence clear and precise.

items.prompt:
Read this short paragraph about a science experiment: 'We mixed the two liquids together. The mixture turned bright blue. My birthday is in July. We recorded the color change in our notebook.' Which sentence should be removed to keep the writing on topic?
A) The mixture turned bright blue.
B) My birthday is in July.
items.answer: B) My birthday is in July.

steps: The paragraph describes the steps and results of a science experiment.
Option A reports a result of the experiment and belongs in the paragraph.
Option B is about a birthday, which has nothing to do with the experiment, so it is off topic and should be removed.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence: 'Due to the fact that it was raining, the game was canceled.' Which revision states the same idea most clearly?
A) Because it was raining, the game was canceled.
B) On account of the rain that was happening, what occurred was that the game ended up being canceled.
items.answer: A) Because it was raining, the game was canceled.

steps: Clear writing states the idea precisely without extra padding words.
Option B adds more wordy phrases ('what occurred was', 'ended up being'), which makes it less clear.
Option A keeps the meaning but replaces 'Due to the fact that' with the simpler 'Because', so it is the clearest revision.
